Google Hotels' first price vs the booking site's total

The number Google Hotels shows a traveler browsing from the United States first beside a booking site is usually not that site's price with taxes: on November 16, 2026, in each of the 11 stays Google priced, out of 12 checked, the same site's price with taxes and fees was 9% to 28% higher than Google's first number (the middle site of each stay). Google labeled it "Nightly price with fees", and in the 4 US stays it equaled the booking site's before-tax price to the dollar; for the hotels outside the US, the gap that visitor saw matched the local hotel tax where we know the rate.

So compare like with like, and before you pay, open the booking site and read the total for your dates. Underbook, a free extension for Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, and the free check on this page (nothing to install) show each booking site's price for your own hotel and dates side by side, with taxes and fees as each site reports them.

The method

How we checked

  • When: November 16, 2026, between 15:39 and 15:46 UTC, and again every week on the same stays.
  • The stays: the same 12 hotels each week, in 12 cities, 2 to 3 nights, 2 adults, check-in 2 to 8 weeks ahead, each priced in its own country and currency.
  • Google Hotels: google.com/travel, from an internet connection in the United States, signed out, a fresh browser for each stay, in English, Google's default view. The number in the table is the one Google shows beside each booking site.
  • The price with taxes: the price with taxes and fees each booking site reports to Google Hotels, read through Underbook's own lookup within 5 seconds of the Google read.

What we could not check

  • We read Google Hotels from the United States. A traveler in another country may be shown a different first number, for example one with taxes where local rules require it; we have not checked that yet.
  • We did not open the booking sites' own pages in this check, so the price with taxes is as each site reports it to Google Hotels; taxes and fees as each site reports them; a resort or destination fee may be extra.
  • Outside the US the sites reported one price to our lookup, with no before-tax price beside it, so for those hotels the link to tax rests on the size of the gap a visitor from the United States saw.
  • At a few sites the two numbers were the same: 7 of the 78 site prices compared.
  • At citizenM New York Times Square, New York, the lowest number on Google's page (KAYAK.com, $443) was on a site our lookup did not list for that stay, so the table uses the lowest site both list.
  • At Rove Downtown, Dubai, the lowest number on Google's page (goseek.com, AED 930) was on a site our lookup did not list for that stay, so the table uses the lowest site both list.
  • At The Grace Hotel, Sydney, the lowest number on Google's page (Agoda, A$274) was on a site our lookup did not list for that stay, so the table uses the lowest site both list.
  • Arpoador Inn, Rio de Janeiro: Google did not open this hotel from its name and city.
  • One read a stay, and 12 hotels picked to spread across cities, chains and independents: a fixed panel to compare week to week, not a survey of all hotels.

What to do with Google Hotels' number

  1. Compare on the same basis. Put Google's number beside another number from Google, or a total beside a total. Google's first number beside another site's price with taxes makes the other site look higher when the offer may be the same.
  2. Open the site and read the total for your dates on the last screen before you pay: taxes and fees as each site reports them; a resort or destination fee may be extra.
  3. Check for a sign-in price. If an offer needs you to enroll or sign in, compare the price you can book signed out too.

Google Hotels prices: common questions

How close is Google Hotels' first price to the booking site's total?+

The number Google Hotels shows a traveler browsing from the United States first beside a booking site is usually not that site's price with taxes: on November 16, 2026, in each of the 11 stays Google priced, out of 12 checked, the same site's price with taxes and fees was 9% to 28% higher than Google's first number (the middle site of each stay). Google labeled it "Nightly price with fees", and in the 4 US stays it equaled the booking site's before-tax price to the dollar; for the hotels outside the US, the gap that visitor saw matched the local hotel tax where we know the rate.

Does Google Hotels include taxes in the price it shows?+

Not in the number it showed first to a traveler browsing from the United States, in our check of November 16, 2026. Google labeled it "Nightly price with fees", and in the 4 US stays it equaled the booking site's before-tax price to the dollar; for the hotels outside the US, the gap that visitor saw matched the local hotel tax where we know the rate. Open the booking site and read the total for your dates before you pay.

Why is the price higher on the booking site than on Google Hotels?+

In our check of November 16, 2026, the gap between Google's first number and the same site's price with taxes and fees matched the local hotel tax where we know the rate: Las Vegas (room tax about 13%), Tokyo (consumption tax 10%) and Sydney (GST 10%). A resort or destination fee may be extra on top.

How often is this checked?+

Every week, on the same 12 stays in 12 cities, signed out. Last checked November 16, 2026.
